entries.abstract: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Radon's Lemma (Johann Radon, 1921) and Helly's Theorem on intersecting families of convex sets (Eduard Helly, 1923; Freek Wiedijk #99) from first principles. Proves that any d + 2 points in ℝ^d admit a Radon partition into two disjoint subsets whose convex hulls intersect, and uses Radon's lemma by induction on the family size to prove Helly's theorem for finite families of convex sets under the general <= d + 1 subfamily intersection hypothesis (covering small families |ι| <= d + 1 as well as large families). To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

entries.abstract: Computing or approximating the permanent is a canonical problem in theoretical computer science and in counting and sampling.  Before this work, the canonical Bethe approximation gave the best known deterministic guarantee, with approximation factor (sqrt 2)^n.  This formalization proves that there is an absolute constant c < sqrt 2 and a deterministic polynomial-time c^n-approximation for every nonnegative rational matrix. It checks the mathematical and algorithmic proof down to Lean's standard logical axioms, including the finite-precision convex-optimization implementation.
entries.title: nimaanari/formalization-beyond-bethe

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of topological semantics for endpoint-varying computational paths.  It constructs both the canonical final composable quotient and the ordinary pullback of quotient arrows.  The selected result proves that the canonical comparison is a continuous bijection and characterizes exactly when it is quotient, a homeomorphism, and an induced topology agreement; under these equivalent conditions ordinary composition is continuous.  It also records discontinuity as an obstruction and proves compact--Hausdorff and discrete sufficient cases.  The selected certificate additionally requires full additive classifications of the genuine based-loop spaces `AddCircle (1 : ℝ)` by `ℤ` and its product torus by `ℤ × ℤ`: the invariant, identity value, composition additivity, explicit standard representatives, and both inverse laws are checked using covering-map lifts and coordinatewise arguments.  It also formalizes the observable based fiber of the universal continuous-path presentation, its homeomorphism to the standard based loop quotient, the final/ordinary pair comparison, and the source-backed Hawaiian-earring transfer: the non-quotient square and discontinuous multiplication force failure of the scoped ordinary-pair quotient, topology agreement, and ordinary multiplication continuity under the comparison.

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the supporting-plane and exact-arithmetic portion of the finite-dimensional argument in Yuhang Shi's research draft on simple zeros of the Riemann zeta function. It proves a conditional scalar two-certificate supporting-plane implication, its explicit piecewise-square-root specialization at block length 219, and the exact strict comparison above 673316977/10^9 for the resulting local assembly expression. The spectral derivation of the trace-envelope alternative, the upstream seven- and nine-point interval certificates, and the analytic passage from finite blocks to a global zeta-zero proportion are not formalized here and are not claimed as Palomar-verified conclusions.

entries.abstract: A standalone Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the finite counterexample to the cost-preserving single-source unsplittable-flow conjecture. The development realizes a directed graph with seven vertices, nine arcs, and three terminal demands; checks a feasible rational fractional flow of cost 58 with maximum demand 15; and proves that every unsplittable routing under the weak additive congestion bound has cost at least 60. It also derives the failure of the strict congestion variant. No general algorithmic or complexity-theoretic claim is made.

entries.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the source-facing polynomial-cube exclusion at actual partial degrees (6,9).  From literal bivariate polynomials of outer degrees six and nine, leading coefficients s^6 and s^9 for a common polynomial s, and nonzero constant Keller bracket, the formalization proves that no such source exists, including when s is constant.  It constructs the finite-pole or infinity expansion, exhausts every timing of the eight Faber loads through rho2, and excludes the remaining elliptic, cusp, zero-invariant, and constant-core terminal fibres.  It does not claim the reduction from an arbitrary Keller pair, all (6,9), maximum eleven, or the plane Jacobian conjecture.

entries.abstract: The Jordan trace form tau(x,y) = tr(L_{x*y}), constructed from the multiplication rather than assumed: symmetric, associative, and positive definite. Symmetry and associativity need neither finite dimensionality nor formal reality; positive definiteness needs both, and runs through the spectral theorem. The carrier is not assumed unital, so this supplies the Euclidean form itself and does not by itself establish a unital Euclidean Jordan algebra. Sits directly on Mathlib's IsCommJordan. Coordinatization is absent. Machine checked, not peer reviewed, no priority claim.

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Nagata's factoriality theorem for noetherian integral domains.  It proves that unique factorization descends from a localization when every denominator is a finite product of prime elements, packages the specialization to submonoids generated by sets of primes, and demonstrates the method with a Nagata-based polynomial UFD theorem.

The Comparator surface contains exactly these three declarations; the other certified results remain supporting proof infrastructure.

entries.abstract: Twenty-one theorems and thirty-three definitions, machine-checked in Lean 4 against Mathlib v4.32.0: the Schwarzschild, Schwarzschild-de Sitter (Kottler), Reissner-Nordstrom (with the Maxwell stress tensor defined and G = 8 pi T proved in all sixteen components), ingoing Vaidya (null dust of rank at most one, rank one wherever dm/dv ≠ 0, for a merely once-differentiable mass function), spatially flat FLRW (both Friedmann equations in Einstein-tensor form), static de Sitter, Minkowski-in-spherical and Kiselev metrics, together with Birkhoff uniqueness in the areal static gauge and the n != 2 equivalence of the two forms of the vacuum equations. The results are classical and NO NEW MATHEMATICS IS CLAIMED: this is a proof of concept for the definitions. Lean checks that a proof establishes a statement, not that a definition means what its name says, so the entry certifies its sign, index and contraction conventions by computing textbook solutions with them -- including four NONZERO answers (de Sitter R = 12/L^2, Reissner-Nordstrom R_thetatheta = Q^2/r^2, Vaidya R_vv = 2 (dm/dv)/r^2, Kiselev R_thetatheta = -3wc r^-(3w+1)), because a curvature definition that was accidentally identically zero would still prove every vacuum theorem here. Scope: everything is a computation in ONE FIXED CHART, an open subset of R^4 -- no atlas, no manifold, no coordinate-independence theorem, no maximal extension, and horizons and coordinate poles lie outside every statement. NOT compared: Ricci symmetry R_bd = R_db in general (it needs Clairaut for the coordinate partial derivative, which Mathlib supplies only for fderiv) or the Bianchi identities; Maxwell's own equations; any matter model, fluid or energy condition beyond the single defined Maxwell stress tensor; non-flat FLRW; the outgoing Vaidya chart. Audience: general relativists, for whom this is the definitional layer a junction-condition or thin-shell statement would be written against, and the formalization community, for whom it is coverage-creating rather than coverage-duplicating. Mathlib v4.32.0 contains no curvature of any kind -- christoffel, ricci, scalarCurvature, Lorentzian, PseudoRiemannian and five further names return zero hits across all 8,264 .lean files at the pinned revision, and its one metric structure hard-codes positive definiteness -- so the entire chain is defined inline in the Challenge.

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the exact evaluation of the normalized 14 by 14 cotangent permanent at p = 29. The formalization proves that its value is 84643985981440 and hence gives a counterexample to the cotangent sign inequality in Zhi-Wei Sun's Conjecture 4.7(ii). It includes the analytic-to-cyclotomic bridge, two separately kernel-checked finite permanent certificates, Chinese-remainder and coefficientwise integer lifting, the Section 3 Archimedean uniqueness argument, and equation (4.1) in the integral cyclotomic quotient.

entries.abstract: Formalizes an exterior-model spinor construction for a field K in which 2 is invertible, using an explicit hyperbolic presentation and the Clifford conjugation action on the ambient quadratic space.  The development proves field-sensitive covering and image results: the positive split-rank spin-to-isometry kernel is {1,-1}, the spin action therefore descends only projectively, the split-line image is exactly the square-scaling subgroup, and a finite-dimensional split Levi element associated to g lies in the ambient spin image exactly when det(g) is a square unit.  The repository also packages the chosen exterior model, half-spin pieces, explicit transvection and square-scaling Clifford lifts, square-class quotient characters, vector-product norm identities, and selected complex and real low-dimensional Clifford classifications.

entries.abstract: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Descartes's Rule of Signs (1637, Wiedijk #73). Proves that for any non-zero real polynomial p(X) over ℝ, the number of positive real roots counted with algebraic multiplicity is bounded above by the number of sign variations in its coefficient sequence (ignoring zero coefficients), and their difference is an even non-negative integer. While the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1) contains the upper-bound inequality in `Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.RuleOfSigns` (`Polynomial.roots_countP_pos_le_signVariations`), this development formalizes the complete two-part theorem by proving the even-parity conclusion (Gauss 1828), establishing the sign-variation parity correspondence with leading and trailing coefficients, and providing a direct list-based coefficient sequence interface.

Arthur Ramos is the first author and responsible maintainer of the Lean formalization; Daniel O. Martinez-Rivillas and Ruy J.G.B. de Queiroz are credited as the mathematical/source authors whose results are formalized.  The Palomar surface uses a restricted Kan-complex exponential and a separate certificate for term-generated semantic bodies, while the substantive repository also formalizes the higher conversion tower and the concrete K-infinity homotopy lambda model.

entries.abstract: A machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the general n-dimensional combinatorial Sperner parity theorem on abstract n-dimensional pseudomanifolds with boundary for arbitrary dimension n : ℕ. Proves the local door-counting parity invariant on (n+1)-simplices, the global double-counting identity on door-facet incidences, and the master parity congruence modulo 2 relating panchromatic (n+1)-simplices to boundary doors. The theorem is conditional on an odd number of boundary (n-1)-doors; obtaining the classical geometric Sperner lemma for simplicial subdivisions of geometric simplices with boundary-preserving colorings is a specialization requiring an additional geometric boundary induction argument not contained in these abstract combinatorial declarations. This n-dimensional development (SpernerND.lean) generalizes and supersedes the fixed-dimensional combinatorial parity identities in the repository's lower-dimensional modules (SpernersLemma.lean and Sperner3D.lean) into a single unified parameterized architecture. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

The project proves that its formal Jacobian determinant is the nonzero constant -2, verifies an explicit three-point fibre over the complex numbers, and derives the failure of injectivity required to refute the dimension-three Jacobian conjecture. The source formulas and proof scope are recorded explicitly; no claim is made about the still-open two-dimensional case.

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of three Poisson-limit statements for the starting points of long constant stretches of an extended Rademacher random completely multiplicative function in a dyadic block, corresponding to the three clauses of Theorem 1.2 in the cited source article. The first proves a total-variation Poisson approximation uniformly over every deterministic mask of the dyadic block. The second gives the Laplace-functional characterization of the limiting spatial Poisson point process. The third gives the corresponding marked characterization together with uniform tightness of the discrete marks. All three compared statements are conditional on exactly three fully stated ordinary propositions specialized from Arratia--Goldstein--Gordon, Evertse--Silverman, and Nicolas--Robin. Those propositions are theorem arguments, not Lean axioms.

entries.abstract: This project formalizes in Lean 4 the statement that the Diophantine equation y*z*(y+z) = x^3 + x^2 + 3x - 1 admits no polynomial parametrization over the rationals whose x-coordinate has degree between 1 and 4. Writing f = X^3 + X^2 + 3X - 1, the compared theorem is that there is no triple of rational polynomials (g, u, v) with g nonconstant of degree at most 4 satisfying the identity u*v*(u+v) = f composed with g. Exhibiting such a family is one of the two standard ways an equation of this shape is settled affirmatively -- the other being a sporadic solution -- and the theorem closes that route at low degree. The statement is over the rationals, which is the stronger reading: an integer family is in particular a rational one, so the theorem also excludes integer families in the same degree range. The statement is unconditional and uses no hypothesis from the literature. Context, stated plainly and without overstatement: this equation is recorded on MathOverflow (question 509449, posed by Bogdan Grechuk) as the smallest cubic equation with open solvability problem under the size ordering H(P) = sum |a_i| 2^{d_i} used in that programme, at H = 35. The compared theorem does NOT decide whether the equation has integer solutions, and makes no claim to. A solution could still exist sporadically, or in a polynomial family whose x-coordinate has degree 5 or more, or the equation could be unsolvable for reasons this theorem does not touch. Degree 5 is not covered and is not claimed: it admits slot-degree shapes the argument for degree at most 4 does not reach, and the bound in the statement is exactly the bound that is proved. The audience is the programme that maintains and closes the frontier list this equation sits on -- Bogdan Grechuk and Ashleigh Ratcliffe, On the shortest open cubic equations (arXiv:2603.29831), and the MathOverflow thread 466803 that tracks the current smallest open equations -- together with the adjacent literature on cubic Diophantine equations of this shape: Janos Kollar and Jennifer Li on the Mordell-Schinzel conjecture for cubic Diophantine equations XYZ = G(X,Y) (arXiv:2412.12080), and Martin Bright and Julian Lyczak on log K3 surfaces (arXiv:1705.04529), whose setting -- a del Pezzo surface minus a smooth anticanonical divisor -- is the geometry of the affine surface defined by this equation. Ruling out low-degree parametric families is directly responsive to how equations on that frontier list are resolved. On novelty: a literature search recorded 2026-07-21 and repeated 2026-08-26 identified no indexed resolution of the equation and no proof-assistant formalization touching it or the frontier list; the search is recorded but not exhaustive, and absence from search is not proof of open status. That search establishes that the equation is open; it does NOT establish that the non-existence of low-degree polynomial families is a new observation, and no such claim is made here. The contribution recorded by this entry is the proof-assistant formalization and its auditable dependency chain.

The translated Metamath proof enters through eleven literal Hailperin sentences, which are used internally as a finite-basis bridge and are proved deductively equivalent to standard NF.

entries.abstract: This project formalizes the odd-exponent branch of Colombo's determinant problem for even matrix size. For every m at least one, every strictly increasing x : Fin (2*m) → ℝ, and every r at least m - 1, it proves that the determinant of the matrix with entries (x_j - x_i)^(2*r+1) is strictly positive. The proof development passes through paired truncated-power determinants, B-spline and Marsden factorization, total nonnegativity, Volterra propagation, and Beta--de Bruijn and Pfaffian identities.

entries.abstract: Answer to Problem 10.32 of the Kourovka Notebook, posed by Yu. I. Merzlyakov in 1986 and still open in the Notebook's 21st edition (2026), in both directions. Positive direction: there are constants C and N0 such that for all nonzero integers r, s with r or s odd, the word x^r y^s is universal on the symmetric group S_n (every permutation is a value) whenever n >= N0 and n >= C * log m(r,s), where m(r,s) is the product of the distinct primes dividing rs. This is the S_n analogue of the logarithmic Brenner-Evans-Silberger bound for A_n; the best previous S_n bound (Droste, 1986) was linear in m. The constant C is effective (the paper gives 4.65 for its fully effective cases), while the threshold N0 is ineffective solely because the proof uses Vinogradov's three-primes theorem. Negative direction, unconditional: the logarithmic shape is optimal. For r = lcm(1..n) with s its odd part, no element of order 3 in S_n is a value of x^r y^s, while log m(r,s) equals theta(n), the full Chebyshev mass of the primes up to n. The proof is machine-checked in Lean 4 on top of Mathlib, with the complete prose write-up included in this repository. The principal theorem, UniversalWords.kourovka_10_32_conditional, is a fully proved implication from eight explicitly stated published theorems (Herzog-Kaplan-Lev, Boccara, three Rosser-Schoenfeld bounds, Montgomery-Vaughan's Brun-Titchmarsh inequality, Vinogradov's three-primes theorem, and the Halberstam-Richert sieve bound) and depends only on Lean's three standard axioms, as does the optimality theorem UniversalWords.not_universal. A quarantined module assumes the eight statements as axioms to recover the unconditional form.

entries.abstract: Formalizes the fundamental group of a finite connected graph, represented as a finite weakly connected directed multigraph with its standard interval-cell quotient realization. The main result identifies the topological fundamental group at a chosen vertex with `FreeGroup (Fin (E + 1 - V))`. The proof compares the topological group with the endomorphism group at the root in Mathlib's free groupoid, whose explicit spanning-tree basis supplies the non-tree-edge generators. The development also proves the cycle-rank identities, root-change equivalences, the tree/triviality criterion, and the corresponding abelianization statement. It constructs a path-lifting quiver and verifies its covering property; the realization of that cover is proved contractible by an explicit quotient homotopy, and path lifting plus monodromy completes the comparison isomorphism.
entries.title: Arthur742Ramos/finite-graph-fundamental-group

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of a quantitative solution to the auxiliary problem suggested by Erdos alongside Problem 1059. Conditional on an explicitly stated standard dimension-one upper-bound sieve theorem, the formalization proves that for every sufficiently large L there are at least ((L+1)!)^eta/(100 log L) integers n in (2L!, (L+1)!] whose prime factors all exceed L and for which n-k! is composite for every 1 <= k <= L. The formalization does not prove that n is prime and therefore does not solve the original Erdos prime problem.

entries.abstract: This project formalizes in Lean 4 a counterexample to a log-concavity conjecture of Coffey and Csordas (Math. Comp. 82 (2013) 2265-2272, Conjecture 2.5, where the quantity below is written S_n), later restated as Open Problem 4.13 of Csordas (Comput. Methods Funct. Theory 15 (2015) 373-391). Let Phi be the kernel of Riemann's integral representation, Phi(u) = sum_{n>=1} (4 pi^2 n^4 e^{9u/2} - 6 pi n^2 e^{5u/2}) e^{-pi n^2 e^{2u}}, and set J_n(t) = (Phi^(n)(t))^2 - Phi^(n-1)(t) Phi^(n+1)(t), the n-th Laguerre expression of Phi. The conjecture asserts J_n(t) > 0 for every real t and every n >= 1. The compared theorem proves J_9(0) < 0, refuting it. The mechanism is a single sign anomaly: Phi is even, so Phi^(9)(0) = 0 and J_9(0) = -Phi^(8)(0) Phi^(10)(0); the expected sign alternation of the even-order derivatives at the origin breaks at order ten, with Phi^(8)(0) and Phi^(10)(0) both positive. The formalization defines Phi through its convergent theta series, uses iterated derivatives, and derives evenness from Mathlib's Gaussian Poisson summation. The audience is the study of Laguerre expressions and Turan-type inequalities for the Riemann kernel: the Csordas school and its successors, who posed the conjecture and restated it as an open problem. The result is a counterexample, checkable directly by anyone with the definition of Phi in hand. This entry makes no claim concerning the Riemann hypothesis and no priority claim for the counterexample. Contemporaneous LLM-assisted exact-certificate proofs of the same sign failure are cited in the source metadata; neither is a proof-assistant formalization. The contribution recorded here is the Lean 4 formalization and its auditable dependency chain. As an aside: the supporting library pinned by this entry also contains machine-checked refutations, on the same axiom set, of conjectures of X.-J. Yang (Fractals 32 (2024) 2340116) asserting that the zeros of the tempered xi function -- the odd channel of this same kernel -- are confined to a single line; those theorems are not compared by this configuration and are mentioned only as context for the library.
entries.title: BrandonMYates/csordas-comparator

entries.abstract: This project formalizes in Lean 4 the zero geometry of the odd channel of Riemann's kernel, refuting conjectures of X.-J. Yang (Fractals 32 (2024) 2340116). Let Phi be the kernel of Riemann's integral representation, Phi(u) = sum_{n>=1} (4 pi^2 n^4 e^{9u/2} - 6 pi n^2 e^{5u/2}) e^{-pi n^2 e^{2u}}, the positive even function whose cosh transform is the completed zeta function, and let F(w) = 2 int_0^infty Phi(u) sinh(wu) du be the odd channel of the same kernel; this is Yang's "tempered xi function", in shifted coordinates. Six statements are compared: F is entire; F has infinitely many zeros; every nonzero zero of F has both real and imaginary parts nonzero; the zeros occur in quartets w, -w, conj w, -conj w; consequently the source paper's Conjecture 1, which asserts that every zero of the tempered xi function lies on the line Re s = 1/2, is false, and indeed apart from the origin no zero lies on that line; and the zeros of the sine channel t -> F(it) are not all real, which is the exactly formalizable content of the source paper's Conjecture 2. The audience is the study of real zeros of Fourier transforms of Riemann's kernel, the line of work of Lagarias and Montague (2011), Ki, Kim and Lee (2009), and the de Bruijn-Newman literature: the weight family interpolating the Lagarias-Montague integrated function and the odd xi derivatives places F at weight zero. Yang's conjectures are the occasion for the formalization, not its research context; Conjecture 1 was also the subject of a prize challenge publicly announced by its author, recorded here solely as evidence that the question was regarded as open and difficult, with no claim made concerning the prize itself. This entry makes no claim concerning the Riemann hypothesis. Scope limitation, stated plainly: the compared theorems quantify over the integral F as defined in the Challenge file. The classical identification of F with the odd part of the completed zeta function is NOT proved in Lean; it was checked numerically only (agreement to about forty digits at several complex points), and nothing in the formal development depends on it. On novelty: the refutation of the source conjectures is believed new. In the literature search completed 26 August 2026, every recorded citation of the source paper is a self-citation, the conjectures are restated as open in a 2026 invited review, and no refutation and no proof-assistant formalization of any compared statement was identified; that search is recorded but not exhaustive, and absence from search is not proof of open status. The component statements are not claimed as new: that F is entire of order one with infinitely many zeros was asserted, without proof, by Yang, Abdel-Aty and Geng (Thermal Science 27 (2023) 505-512) for this same function; the exclusion of zeros from the imaginary axis is, in sine-transform coordinates, a 1971 theorem of Spira, independently reproved here, with classical ancestry in Polya (1918, 1926) and Wintner (1935); and the quartet symmetry is recorded as a printed remark by Lagarias and Montague for the sibling weight family. The contribution recorded here is the proof-assistant formalization and its auditable dependency chain. As an aside: the supporting library pinned by this entry also contains a machine-checked counterexample, on the same axiom set, to a log-concavity conjecture of Coffey and Csordas for the derivatives of this same kernel; that theorem is not compared by this configuration and is mentioned only as context for the library.

A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the Sylvester–Gallai theorem (J. J. Sylvester 1893, T. Gallai 1944, L. M. Kelly 1948; Freek Wiedijk #98). Proves that every finite non-collinear set of points in the real Euclidean plane contains an ordinary line passing through exactly two points of the set, formalized via Kelly's minimal point-line distance argument.

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of the first two moments and variance of the number of long constant-stretch starts of an extended Rademacher random completely multiplicative function in a dyadic block, together with the quantitative exponential estimate for the separated homogeneous two-start sum. Uniformly in the critical window, Theorem 1.4 gives the first-moment rate, second falling-factorial-moment convergence, R_2(N,L)=o_C(N^2), and variance convergence; Corollary 11.3 gives the stronger bound R_2(N,L) <<_C N^2 exp(-c_R sqrt(log N)/log log N) for some c_R>0. Both compared statements are conditional on exactly two fully stated ordinary propositions specialized from Evertse--Silverman and Nicolas--Robin. Those propositions are theorem arguments, not Lean axioms.

entries.abstract: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the Friendship Theorem (P. Erdős, A. Rényi, and V. T. Sós, 1966; H. S. Wilf, 1971). Proves that any finite simple graph on at least three vertices (|V| ≥ 3) in which every pair of distinct vertices shares exactly one common neighbor must contain a universal vertex (the 'politician'), structuring the graph as a collection of triangles sharing a central vertex (a windmill graph). entries.abstract: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of J. A. Bondy's 1972 theorem on induced subsets. Proves that for any family F of n distinct subsets of an arbitrary finite ground set X, there exists a distinguishing subset S ⊆ X of cardinality at most n - 1 such that the restriction map s ↦ s ∩ S is injective on F. entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of an explicit construction for the Furstenberg-Sárközy problem. If D(N) is the largest size of a subset of {1,...,N} with no nonzero square difference, the development proves that an explicit eleven-block constant alphaInf is at most liminf log D(N)/log N, that every exponent below alphaInf holds eventually pointwise, and that 0.7537 < alphaInf. The proof includes the finite certificates, the composite even-digit lift, CRT gluing, asymptotic passage, and kernel-checked numerical inequalities. This strictly improves Krachun's preceding explicit exponent 0.752796455874514... and moves the lower bound farther beyond 3/4.

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the existence assertion in Theorem 1.1 of arXiv:2608.12280v1 with the sharp constant K = 1: for every countable Bessel sequence with bound 1 in a complex Hilbert space, there exist measurable functions on the unit interval, pointwise bounded by 1, whose correlations reproduce the sequence's Gram matrix. This solves an open problem posed by Olevskii.

entries.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of a two-sheet implication in the aligned nontrivial cubic-Kummer analysis at actual partial degrees (6,9). Every field-valued solution of the four lower-Pfaffian invariant equations is proved to lie on a common-power sheet with zero source bracket or on an elliptic sheet; converse inclusions and existence of the sheets are not compared.  The formalization derives the elliptic equation and terminal one-form, excludes nonconstant reduced rational trajectories on its C != 0 fibre by a finite forbidden-value argument, factors the C=0 fibre, and verifies the shifted Davenport--Stothers bracket and terminal descent. Version 2 derives the finite-place valuation classification directly from the reduced rational ODE, proves the one-point support theorem, and excludes that sheet in the noncube Kummer branch.  It does not claim the preceding landing from an arbitrary Keller pair, the cube branch, all (6,9), maximum eleven, or JC2.

entries.abstract: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the Graham–Pollak theorem (1971) and its tightness on complete bipartite partitions of complete graphs. Proves that any partition of the edges of the complete graph K_n into m complete bipartite subgraphs requires at least n - 1 bipartite graphs (m >= n - 1), adapting Helge Tverberg's 1982 linear-algebraic quadratic form argument. Also formalizes the canonical star partition proving tightness. To the maintainers' knowledge, Graham–Pollak was not previously formalized in Mathlib (checked against Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

entries.abstract: Let N(T,2T) count the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function with ordinate in (T,2T], with multiplicity, and N_0^s(T,2T) the simple zeros among them on the critical line. The Lean development accompanying arXiv:2608.13637 (anthropics/zeta-23-lean) proves, for Mathlib's riemannZeta and unconditionally, that for every eps > 0 and all large T, (H - eps) N(T,2T) <= N_0^s(T,2T), with H = 3/2 - (1/sqrt 2) cot(1/sqrt 2) = 0.67250070367941164573... (its Theorem D). Ainta (github.com/ainta/zeta-simple-zeros) refines H by carrying the spectral defect of the Gram matrix of the simple-zero vectors through that argument and bounding it block by block through a local inequality on seven points. Advertised here: that refinement carried out for n points at once, and three instances. Parametrically, for n >= 2, c > 0, m >= n, p > 0 with c(m-(n-1)) <= 1, if c <= F(n,p,g) for every nonnegative vector g of n-1 gaps (the hypothesis hCert), then for every eps > 0 and all large T, (Phi_n(n,c,m,p) - eps) N(T,2T) <= N_0^s(T,2T), where Phi_n(n,c,m,p) = (H - (n-1)(m-1)/(pm)) / (1 - c(m-(n-1))/m). At n = 7 this is Ainta's theorem. THE THREE-POINT INSTANCE IS UNCONDITIONAL. At (n,c,p) = (3, 1345/10^6, 3000) the hypothesis is proved, not assumed: the overlap weight w = k^2 is enclosed from a twelve-term Taylor bound on cos and sin and the closed form of the kernel, and 368 interval cell lemmas over rationals, applied 1515 times over 487 leaves, cover the quarter-plane of the two gaps. No external interval-arithmetic certificate is assumed for the three-point theorem, and no floating point appears. The cap gives m = 745 and the constant (149000000 H - 99200)/148800133 = 0.67273733450380945875..., exceeding H by 2.3663e-4: for Mathlib's riemannZeta, an unconditional improvement of the dependency's Theorem D. THE FOUR-POINT INSTANCE IS ALSO UNCONDITIONAL. At (n,c,p) = (4, 2310/10^6, 2500), the finite inequality at every triple of nonnegative gaps is proved inside Lean. The cap gives m = 435 and the resulting constant is (906250 H - 1085)/904171 = 0.67284701976668870316.... The bound and ratio carry no certificate hypothesis and use exactly the same three permitted axioms. The eight-point instance stays conditional. Our n-point generalisation of Ainta's interval verifier accepts c = 41763/10^7 at p = 3200, giving m = 246 and 0.67305298298962888...; interval-arithmetic acceptance is not a Lean proof, so hCert remains explicit. The contrast is explicit in the statements: the parametric and eight-point theorems retain a named certificate hypothesis, while the three- and four-point theorems prove their certificates inside Lean.

In an equivalent polynomial-growth coefficient model, it proves that the −1 and i Fourier eigenspaces vanish, identifies the surviving 1 and −i eigenspaces as one-dimensional lines generated by explicit generalized eta products up to the respective thresholds θ ≤ 1/8 and θ ≤ 3/8, and proves that the full admissible space has dimension 2, 1, or 0 in the resulting three θ ranges.

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / mathlib formalization of Dana Scott's 1980 Oxford lectures, published May 1981 as PRG-19 Lectures on a Mathematical Theory of Computation. The principal sourced Palomar result is the first sentence of Theorem 8.8: the neighbourhood system U over [0,1) ⊆ ℚ is universal, in the sense that every countable neighbourhood system D embeds as a subdomain (D ⊴ U). Comparator also selects two new formal corollaries: P4_embeds for Scott's Example 1.5 and Ssys_embeds for Exercise 7.22. Scott defines those systems but does not separately state the embeddings. This foundational universality result supplies a concrete host for all countable domains; it is relevant to domain theory, denotational semantics, mathematical logic, and formalized mathematics. entries.abstract:
A Euclidean Jordan algebra is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space carrying a commutative bilinear product with a unit, satisfying the Jordan identity (x*y)*(x*x) = x*(y*(x*x)) and the associativity of the inner product <x*y, z> = <y, x*z>. This is Faraut-Koranyi's definition (Analysis on Symmetric Cones, III.1). This development formalizes the classical structure theory of these algebras.
Mathlib carries the Jordan identity as the typeclass IsCommJordan together with five operator-commutation lemmas, and nothing beyond that: no idempotent theory, no Peirce decomposition, no spectral theory. This development supplies that layer.
The registered results, in four separate Comparator configurations. (1) The Koecher / Alfsen-Shultz theorem: a unital linear order isomorphism of a Euclidean Jordan algebra is a Jordan automorphism, with the cone taken to be the sums-of-squares cone and the product carried as a bundled bilinear map so that the statement needs no ring instance to elaborate. (2) The single-element spectral theorem: every element of a finite-dimensional formally real Jordan algebra is a real linear combination of a complete family of pairwise-orthogonal idempotents. Finite-dimensionality is load-bearing rather than decorative - the polynomial algebra R[X] satisfies every other hypothesis and has no nonconstant spectral resolution. (3) The Jordan trace form tau(x,y) = tr(L_{x*y}): symmetric, associative, and positive definite, constructed from the multiplication alone rather than assumed. Symmetry and associativity are registered at their honest generality, which does not include finite-dimensionality; positive definiteness needs the spectral theorem and therefore does. (4) The frame Peirce decomposition: for a Jordan frame p_1, ..., p_n the algebra is the internal direct sum of the blocks V_ij over unordered pairs, together with the Faraut-Koranyi table entry dim V_ii = 1.
Direction and scope. Every registered theorem is proved outright from the stated hypotheses; none is conditional on a cited result. The development also proves, but does not register here, Albert's power-associativity theorem (x^(m+1) * x^(n+1) = x^(m+n+2), with no unit, finite dimension, formal reality or positivity assumed), which is registered from a separate development of the author's and is deliberately not re-registered; the existence of a Jordan frame in any nontrivial finite-dimensional Euclidean Jordan algebra; the associativity of the subalgebra generated by a single element; the Peirce subalgebras J_2(c) and J_0(c) as Euclidean Jordan algebras in their own right; and an order-unit-space structure with the sums-of-squares cone, proved to coincide with the Loewner order on the concrete carrier.
What is NOT here. Coordinatization is absent: the Jordan-von Neumann-Wigner route continues by making the off-diagonal block a composition algebra and applying Hurwitz's theorem to land J = H_n(K), and that step depends on the composition-algebra classification, which lives in a separate repository. This development therefore stops at the connectors and the frame-block structure. There is no functional calculus on the spectral resolution. Frame conjugacy (Faraut-Koranyi IV.2.5) is not proved - the development sidesteps it by carrying a Jordan frame as data rather than reasoning about the rank as a number. The classification of simple Euclidean Jordan algebras is not proved, and no statement about the exceptional algebra H_3(O) appears. Formal reality and the associativity of the inner product are equivalent over R in finite dimension, but that equivalence is not formalized, so both appear as hypotheses.
The abstract theory has a live carrier: H_n(K) for K = R or C, the Hermitian matrices under A*B = (AB+BA)/2, is an instance of the EuclideanJordanAlgebra class, checked by instance synthesis in the mechanical audit rather than by inspection. The check is finer than nonemptiness of the class: every Peirce rule mentioning the half-eigenspace would be vacuously true on a carrier where that space is trivial, and it is trivial for the two idempotents one reaches for first, so a witness with nonzero half-eigenspace is exhibited on H_2(C).
Every declaration in the tracked tree has an axiom closure contained in Lean's three core axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The tree carries no custom axiom, no sorry and no native_decide.

The development also proves, but does not register here, Albert's power-associativity theorem (x^(m+1) * x^(n+1) = x^(m+n+2), with no unit, finite dimension, formal reality or positivity assumed), which is registered from a separate development of the author's and is deliberately not re-registered; the existence of a Jordan frame in any nontrivial finite-dimensional Euclidean Jordan algebra; the associativity of the subalgebra generated by a single element; the Peirce subalgebras J_2(c) and J_0(c) as Euclidean Jordan algebras in their own right; and an order-unit-space structure with the sums-of-squares cone, proved to coincide with the Loewner order on the concrete carrier.
What is NOT here. Coordinatization is absent: the Jordan-von Neumann-Wigner route continues by making the off-diagonal block a composition algebra and applying Hurwitz's theorem to land J = H_n(K), and that step depends on the composition-algebra classification, which lives in a separate repository. This development therefore stops at the connectors and the frame-block structure. There is no functional calculus on the spectral resolution. Frame conjugacy (Faraut-Koranyi IV.2.5) is not proved - the development sidesteps it by carrying a Jordan frame as data rather than reasoning about the rank as a number. The classification of simple Euclidean Jordan algebras is not proved, and no statement about the exceptional algebra H_3(O) appears. Formal reality and the associativity of the inner product are equivalent over R in finite dimension, but that equivalence is not formalized, so both appear as hypotheses.
The abstract theory has a live carrier: H_n(K) for K = R or C, the Hermitian matrices under A*B = (AB+BA)/2, is an instance of the EuclideanJordanAlgebra class, checked by instance synthesis in the mechanical audit rather than by inspection. The check is finer than nonemptiness of the class: every Peirce rule mentioning the half-eigenspace would be vacuously true on a carrier where that space is trivial, and it is trivial for the two idempotents one reaches for first, so a witness with nonzero half-eigenspace is exhibited on H_2(C).
Every declaration in the tracked tree has an axiom closure contained in Lean's three core axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The tree carries no custom axiom, no sorry and no native_decide.

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of three sparse oblivious-subspace-embedding results at the Nelson--Nguyen parameter scale: the fully independent signed-hash SparseStack construction, independent uniform signed exact-s columns, and a limited-independence transfer for finite laws whose combined hash-sign selector marginals agree with SparseStack through order 4q.  At the stated rounded parameters the selected theorems give failure probability at most delta, with explicit strict bounds s < 1356 q / epsilon and m < 306456 (d + q) / epsilon^2 where those parameter conclusions are packaged.  The formalization is machine checked but has not been peer reviewed and makes no priority claim.
entries.title: DiarHaidary/Nelson-Nguyen-conjecture-upper-bound-palomar

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of square maximality for spanning trees of induced subgraphs of the square lattice. For every positive integer n and every finite set S of n^2 points in Z^2, the induced lattice graph on S has at most as many spanning trees as the n by n square, with equality exactly when S is a translate of that square. The development also proves the corresponding strict and equality statements for arbitrary spanning subgraphs, together with the finite Matrix--Tree theorem and the proof chain used by the paper.
entries.title: novou/square-maximality-palomar

entries.abstract: For a fixed angular radius theta in (0, pi/2), the least number M(n, theta) of spherical caps of angular radius theta, centred at points of the unit sphere of R^n, whose union is that whole sphere satisfies (1/n) log M(n, theta) -> -log sin theta as n -> infinity. This is the covering half of Wyner (1967): the elementary volume bound gives the lower bound on the covering number and a random-covering argument gives the upper bound. The statement is given in Mathlib's own vocabulary, as an asymptotic for Metric.coveringNumber of Metric.sphere 0 1 in EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) at chordal radius 2 sin (theta/2), and introduces no definition of its own; two compared lemmas establish that an angular cap of half-angle theta about a unit vector is exactly the closed chordal ball of that radius, which is what licenses reading the result as a statement about caps. Two further compared theorems rule out the junk values that the N-infinity-valued covering number and the logarithm would otherwise admit.
entries.title: geoconuk/lean-misc-math

entries.abstract:
A Lean 4 formalisation of *Uniform sheafy Tate rings that are not stably uniform* (Birkbeck–Torzewski), answering Question 7 of Kedlaya's *Nonarchimedean Scottish Book* in the negative: a sheafy uniform Huber pair need not be stably uniform. Buzzard–Verberkmoes and Mihara proved that stably uniform Tate Huber rings are sheafy; whether the converse holds was open.
The paper gives two complete Tate algebras over a complete discretely valued field `k` that are uniform, nonnoetherian integral domains with `A° = A₀`, strongly sheafy (every Tate algebra `A⟨X₁, …, Xₙ⟩` is sheafy), and yet not stably uniform, because an explicit rational localisation is not uniform. The first (Theorem 1.1) is the finite-jet pinching algebra `𝓐 = B ×_D C`, the pullback of a Milnor square with `B = k⟨W, Q⟩/(Q²)`, `C = k⟨W, W⁻¹⟩⟨Q⟩`, `D = C/(Q²)` — concretely, the series in `k⟨W, W⁻¹⟩⟨Q⟩` whose `Q⁰`- and `Q¹`-coefficients have nonnegative `W`-support; its bad chart `𝓐⟨W/ϖ⟩ ≅ k⟨X, Q⟩/(Q²)` is non-reduced. The second (Theorem 8.1) is the weighted-parity algebra `𝒜_w`, whose bad chart is an integral domain; the paper proves it for every unbounded weight `w ≥ 1`, the formalisation for `w(n) = n`.
This submission certifies the seven conclusions of Theorem 1.1 together with two statements ruling out a vacuous reading of its sheafiness claims, stated self-containedly on Mathlib in `Challenge.lean` over an arbitrary complete ultrametric field with DVR valuation ring; Theorem 8.1 is certified by the repository's in-library configuration. The repository also develops the surrounding theory after Wedhorn's *Adic Spaces*: Huber and Tate rings, the adic spectrum, rational localisations, the structure presheaf, and sheafiness (Definition 8.26), including the strongly noetherian theorem (8.28(b)).
entries.title: CBirkbeck/uniform-sheafy-tate-domains-lean

entries.abstract: For an explicitly defined difference B of two signed cone theta series over Q(sqrt(5)), Lean proves a closed nonmultiplicativity witness and a complete prime-index classification. For every rational prime p congruent to 1 modulo 10, B((p-1)/10) is one of -2, -1, 1, 2; a norm-negative golden integer generator and its strict fundamental-window normalization exist; and the coefficient has magnitude two exactly when the resulting geometric residue invariant is one modulo three. The invariant is also proved independent of the generator within the explicitly defined signed fundamental-unit orbit.
entries.title: xiangyazi24/palomar-qseries-prime-coefficients

entries.abstract:
We prove the following mod-2 identity for real symplectic Banach spaces:
  If $(X, \omega)$ is a real symplectic Banach space, and $T \in L(X)$ satisfies:
    (1) $I + T^+T$ is Fredholm
    (2) $I + T^2$ has finite rank
  Then
    $\rank(T^2 + I) \equiv \dim \ker (I + T^+T) \pmod 2$.
In the above, $T^+$ represents the symplectic adjoint. See our paper for more depth in definitions. This identity is applied to show that no hyperplane of the real Kalton-Peck space has a complex structure. We note that in our notation, a symplectic Banach space always assumes that the symplectic form \omega is a strong symplectic form. See our paper for more detail on the definitions.
We formalize:
 (1) The mod-2 identity for arbitrary real symplectic Banach spaces
 (2) An application of the identity to show that if $T \in L(Z_2)$ and $T^2 + I$ has finite rank, then $T^2 + I$ has even rank.
     Here, Z_2 is the real Kalton-Peck space.
 (3) The corollary that no hyperplane of the real Kalton-Peck space has a complex structure.
entries.title: adas1236/KaltonPeckPalomar

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of all sixteen units of Mishnah Kinnim, with a machine-checked physical optimization theorem for the Koppel--Reiss reading of Kinnim 3:2. For any list of pair counts grouped by owner, the priest has already acted on exactly half of the mixed birds above and half below. A physical world records one action level for every individual bird of every owner. Lean proves that every such world is compatible, by permutation, with the fixed half-split action list. Counting valid birds directly from each owner's closed-pair quota, the theorem proves that the exact minimum over all physical apportionments is twice the complement of the largest attainable subset sum not exceeding half the total, and constructs an apportionment attaining it. The repository also covers all sixteen units, flight recurrences, and replacement-inventory covers.
entries.title: ashebson/kinin-lean

entries.abstract:
A sequential product on the effects of an order-unit space is a binary operation a & b, read "first test a, then test b with the state updated by the first test", satisfying the seven axioms S1-S7 of van de Wetering (arXiv:1803.11139, Definition 2). This development registers two classification theorems for such products on the Hermitian matrix algebras.
On H_N(R), the Hermitian N x N real matrices with N >= 1, every sequential product is the Lueders product sqrt(a) b sqrt(a): there is no free parameter. On H_N(C) with N >= 3, every sequential product has the twist normal form a^(1/2+it) b a^(1/2-it) for a unique real t. The twist family is a one-parameter deformation of the Lueders product, and the complex theorem says nothing outside it satisfies the axioms.
Prior art. That Lueders is not the only sequential product, and twisted products of this shape in particular, are not new: Gudder asked the question in 2005, Shen and Wu answered it negatively and gave a general construction in 2009 (arXiv:0905.0596), and Liu, Wu and Wu showed those examples are unitary equivalent to Lueders (arXiv:1009.2593). What is registered here is the converse direction. The examples are not exhibited; they are shown to be forced, with the parameter unique, and with no product outside the family admissible. The equations are asserted on all effects, including singular ones, and the uniqueness of t is part of the registered statement.
Direction. Both registered classification theorems are necessity: a product satisfying the axioms is supplied, and the theorem says it has the stated normal form. The two converses differ in status and neither is registered. For the complex case, that each real t defines a SeqProd satisfying S2 is proved in the wider development; together with the registered uniqueness it is what would make the parameter map injective. For the real case, that the Lueders formula defines a SeqProd satisfying S2 is not proved anywhere in this development. Nothing here registers a bijection between parameters and products, or the admissibility of the Lueders formula.
The package also registers two classical theorems the development proves in passing. Albert's power-associativity theorem: in a commutative Jordan ring carrying an R-module structure, x^(m+1) * x^(n+1) = x^(m+n+2), with no unit, finite dimension, formal reality or positivity assumed. And the real case of Wigner's theorem: every transition probability preserving self-map of the rays of a finite-dimensional real inner product space is induced by a linear isometry, with bijectivity not assumed but derived.
Both classification theorems are proved from S1-S7 with no hypotheses beyond the dimension bounds, and their axiom closures contain only Lean's three core axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The continuity axiom S2 is stated in the order-unit norm, as an explicit epsilon-delta condition, so the statement file depends on no normed-space or topological instance; the equivalence with continuity in the carrier's Frobenius topology is proved in the development.
Scope. The repository carries three Comparator configurations, selecting four theorems between them: the two sequential-product classifications above, which use the SeqProd interface and the axiom S2 and correspond to numbered rows of the manuscript; and the two ancillary classical theorems, Albert and Wigner, which use neither and correspond to no manuscript row. Each configuration is a separate submission and a separate entry; no one entry contains all four. No Palomar claim is made here for any other declaration in the repository.
The two classification theorems are two rows of a thirty-six row manifest tracking the numbered results of the accompanying manuscript. The manuscript as a whole is not formalized: as of 2026-08-12 the manifest stands at 12 rows formalized, 19 partial, and 5 absent. In particular the quaternionic row H_n(H) and the Albert-algebra row H_3(O) of the manuscript's main theorem are not proved here, and the coalescence and diagonal-homomorphism lemmas are established on the concrete carrier H_N(C) rather than at the manuscript's stated generality of a finite-dimensional simple Euclidean Jordan algebra.
entries.title: ehrlich-b/sequential-products-lean

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of a residual-or-unmatched barrier for local Möbius cancellation. At every sufficiently large fixed-band scale, either the permitted edge length reaches the retained-prime product or every member of an explicit squarefree prime-product family is unmatched. Chebyshev estimates give the exact binomial and factorial population bounds. The product scale also converts residual rank to its logarithmic threshold with the exact limiting constant.
entries.title: mbaccaro-dev/mathematical-proofs

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the global power-of-two balance connecting dyadic defect, block variation, and positive Möbius-logarithm prefix energy. Eventual nonnegativity on exactly those dyadic blocks gives an explicit all-endpoint cubic energy bound. With the stated weighted-squarefree remainder estimate, the formalization also recovers the sharp 6/pi^2 leading coefficient and retains the complete finite-prefix correction.
entries.title: mbaccaro-dev/mathematical-proofs

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 verification of the coefficientwise Kronecker partial-fraction identity and the general boundary-cleared Hickerson--Mortenson Hecke--Appell identity for f_{n,n+p,n}, for all positive integers n and p.
entries.title: xiangyazi24/palomar-hahn-hecke-appell

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the sequence-level conditioning construction for Selberg divisor feedback. Two explicit perturbations of the von Mangoldt weight stay in the positive prime-power cone, approximate the divisor data to an arbitrary tolerance through twice the observation scale, separate their summatory outputs at a near-linear power scale, and retain one uniform linear Selberg bound.
entries.title: mbaccaro-dev/mathematical-proofs

entries.abstract: Machine-checked Lean 4 proofs of solved research problems from the Erdős problems collection, hosted as stable formal_proof targets for Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures. The principal result is an affirmative answer to Erdős Problem #730 (Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa and Straus, 1975): the set of pairs n < m for which binom(2n, n) and binom(2m, m) have the same set of prime divisors is infinite, and in fact contains infinitely many consecutive pairs (n, n + 1). The proof formalises the argument posted informally by Liam Price on the problem's discussion page on 24 June 2026: Kummer's theorem converts equality of prime supports into a base-p digit condition, an explicit quadratic family of consecutive pairs is constructed, a fixed-depth Fourier estimate bounds the digit obstruction on blocks of length p^r, a uniform depth tail uses a Mertens-type reciprocal-prime input, the top-prime range is handled by fixed-modulus divisor switching using the prime number theorem in arithmetic progressions, and an exact rational density budget yields positive lower density and hence infinitude. The repository also proves the sumset form of Erdős Problem #154 (equidistribution of A + A in residue classes for Sidon sets A with |A| ~ sqrt N, from Lindström's theorem) and hosts smaller bounded results for Problems #94, #399 and #1074. Every tracked theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; each registry statement under Palomar/ restates its result in a Challenge importing Mathlib alone.
entries.title: williamjblair/lean-proofs

entries.abstract: Davenport and Heilbronn (1936) exhibited a Dirichlet series with real coefficients satisfying a Riemann-type functional equation which nevertheless has zeros off the critical line. It is the standard demonstration that a functional equation of Riemann type does not on its own force the Riemann Hypothesis, it is the reference counterexample against which structural explanations of the Riemann Hypothesis are tested, and the location of its zeros remains an active subject. The function is DH(s) = (1 - i*kappa)/2 * L(s, chi) + (1 + i*kappa)/2 * L(s, chi^-1) for a quartic Dirichlet character chi mod 5 and kappa = (sqrt(10 - 2*sqrt 5) - 2)/(sqrt 5 - 1), the value that rotates the two conjugate root numbers onto each other and so makes the Dirichlet coefficients real. This submission advertises one theorem, the analytic half of the Davenport-Heilbronn theorem: there exists an entire function represented by the Davenport-Heilbronn Dirichlet series on Re z > 1 whose completion (pi/5)^(-(s+1)/2) * Gamma((s+1)/2) * f(s) is symmetric under s -> 1-s. The statement is existential in f, so it carries its own non-vacuity and needs none of the character theory used to construct the witness. What the work consists of. The Davenport-Heilbronn function is not a library object anywhere we could find, so the development builds it: the quartic character mod 5, the linear combination, entirety on all of C, the identification of the Dirichlet coefficients as the real period-5 sequence 1, kappa, -kappa, -1, 0, and the completed functional equation. The last of these is where the content sits. It reduces to a root-number identity whose convention-sensitive constants are derived inside the development, from Mathlib's Real.cos_pi_div_five by radical algebra, rather than transcribed from a table; the standard sources state kappa without deriving it in a form a kernel will accept, and getting it wrong yields a function whose coefficients are not real and which therefore is not the counterexample. The functional equation is stated with explicit guards excluding the poles of the two Gamma factors, because Mathlib's junk value Gamma = 0 at the poles would otherwise make the unrestricted equation false for reasons having nothing to do with the mathematics. Audience. The Davenport-Heilbronn function is a named object of analytic number theory with a continuing literature on its zeros, so a machine-checked construction of it is of direct interest to number theorists working on zeros of L-functions and on what a Riemann-type functional equation does and does not imply. It is also the object a formalized treatment of the Davenport-Heilbronn theorem has to have before it can say anything, and this supplies it in a form that carries its own non-vacuity. Prior art. A search of Mathlib at the revision pinned by this repository found no Davenport-Heilbronn function and no formalization of this functional equation. That is a bounded search of one library. No systematic search of other proof assistants or of the mathematical literature for prior formalizations has been run, and no novelty against the literature is claimed: the mathematics is Davenport and Heilbronn's, published in 1936. Scope. The Davenport-Heilbronn theorem itself is NOT proved here. Its full statement additionally requires a zero s with Re s different from 1/2, and that conjunct appears nowhere in the advertised theorem. What is offered is the analytic half alone. No numerical enclosure for any zero of DH is asserted, and nothing here is a statement about the Riemann zeta function or the Riemann Hypothesis.

entries.abstract: A self-contained version of the formal-conjectures formalization by Paul Lezeau and Dean Cureton. It disproves the generalized Jacobian conjecture over every nontrivial commutative ring using an explicit determinant-one polynomial self-map in three variables. The formal-conjectures formalisation remains the reference statement.

entries.abstract: Formalizes the prime-local obstruction by proving the sharp threshold for each local block, divergence of the associated von Mangoldt and prime-power budgets, and divergence of every scalar budget satisfying the sharp pointwise lower bound at every natural-number index.

entries.abstract: A variational identity for the Fredholm operator A = I + T on the interval I = [-1/2, 1/2], where T is convolution against the Farmer-Gonek-Lee pair-correlation form factor F1(x) = |x| - 4x^2 + sum_k a_k |x|^(2k+3) with a_k = 2^(2k+3) k! / (2k+2)!. Let w = A^(-1)1 and c* = <1, A^(-1)1>. Over the source-admissible class of scalar profiles v(s) = phi(Ls)^2 induced by even, radially nonincreasing C^2 windows supported exactly on [-L/2, L/2] with 0 <= phi <= 1 and uniform L^1 bounds on phi'' and (phi^2)'', the supremum of <1,v>^2 / <Av,v> equals c*, and the infimum of the reciprocal quotient <Av,v> / <1,v>^2 equals 1/c*. The upper bound <1,v>^2 <= c* <Av,v> is energy Cauchy-Schwarz. It holds for every v, it is classical, and it is not the content of this result. The content is the reverse inequality over the constrained class: c* is the value of the unconstrained variational problem, and the identity says that imposing evenness, radial monotonicity, an exact compact support, the amplitude ceiling 0 <= phi <= 1 and uniform L^1 bounds on the second derivatives does not lower the supremum. That direction is proved by exhibiting an explicit endpoint-tapered family inside the class, indexed by the scale L, whose quotient converges to c*. Both orientations are advertised because the orientation is load-bearing: it is the quotient with <1,v>^2 in the numerator whose supremum is c*, and the supporting development also proves that the two are not interchangeable. The advertised statement is existential in the profile and in the two uniform constants, so it carries its own non-vacuity: an IsLUB or IsGLB assertion over the image of an empty class is unsatisfiable in the reals, so the theorem cannot hold unless the class is populated by the constants for which it is stated. Audience. The kernel F1 is the pair-correlation form factor and the window class is the generalized, load-bearing class of Section 7.1 of the cited paper rather than a convenient flat-topped realization, so the constrained supremum settled here is the quantity that a critical-line proportion argument built on that framework optimizes; analytic number theorists working on the proportion of zeros of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line, and on pair correlation of its zeros, are the audience for which the exact value of that supremum over the admissible class, rather than a bound on it, is the relevant fact. The statement is also a closure result for a constrained admissible class in the variational theory of Fredholm integral operators (MSC 45B05, 49R05) and can be read there without reference to its origin. What the theorem itself asserts is bounded by the scope field below: it is a statement about a Fredholm operator on an interval and a class of test profiles, and it is evidence for nothing beyond that.

entries.abstract: Machine-checked proofs of three probabilistic convergence theorems for restarted Minimal Polynomial Extrapolation (MPE) applied to nonlinear fixed-point iterations.  Dithered restarts keep the error below the doubly exponential schedule delta^(theta^m), for any theta in (1,2), from every starting point -- the breakdown set included -- with an explicit failure-probability exponent over the dither; in the root sense the convergence order is at least theta.  Under simple spectrum, the error follows a quadratically shrinking dither schedule (root order at least 2) with failure probability linear in the initial radius up to a logarithmic factor, and MPE coincides with Reduced Rank Extrapolation at every cycle. With no dither at all, the restarted iteration from a single uniformly random starting point at worst squares the error at every cycle with high probability, under two checkable hypotheses on the Jacobian and the quadratic Taylor coefficients.  The registered statements are self-contained over mathlib: every object of the construction is introduced by an explicit defining equation among the hypotheses.
entries.title: sloisel/MPE-Formal

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, against Mathlib, of the Kovač–Tao resolution of Erdős problem #266 (a conjecture of Stolarsky): it is not true that every sequence of positive integers with convergent reciprocal sum admits an integer shift t >= 1 making the shifted Ahmes series irrational.  The stronger construction is also formalized: a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers whose shifted series has a rational sum for every admissible rational shift.

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of a quantitative Poisson approximation for the starting points of long constant stretches of an extended Rademacher random completely multiplicative function in a dyadic block. The compared theorem uses a finite prime-sign cylinder and proves, uniformly in the critical window |L - log_2 N| <= C, that the total-variation distance to Pois(N/2^L) is O_C((log log N)^-2). It is conditional on three fully stated ordinary propositions specialized from Arratia--Goldstein--Gordon, Evertse--Silverman, and Nicolas--Robin; those propositions are theorem arguments, not Lean axioms.

entries.abstract: Formal proof of the First Cuboid Conjecture, which states that for all positive coprime integers a, b with a ≠ b, a certain degree-8 polynomial P_{a,b}(t) over ℤ is irreducible. This conjecture was proposed by Shapirov in "Perfect cuboids and irreducible polynomials" (arXiv:1108.5348) as part of a family of three conjectures whose combined truth would imply the nonexistence of a perfect Euler brick. The proof first analyses rational factors and the symmetry F(−x) vs F(x) to reduce irreducibility of the degree-8 polynomial to irreducibility of a degree-4 factor Q_{a,b}, and the coprime branch to a Diophantine identity. Irreducibility of Q is in turn reduced to the quartic Diophantine equation x⁴ + 34x²y² + y⁴ = z², whose only trivial solutions are established by Fermat-style infinite descent. The formal proof was autonomously discovered by the AlphaProof Nexus agent; an independent informal proof using rank-zero elliptic curves was given by Asiryan (arXiv:2510.11768).

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of an exact enumeration identity and two consequences: for a finite type α, the number of families B ⊆ Set α that are topological bases equals the sum, over all topologies τ on α, of 2^(|τ| − |M_τ|), where M_τ is the canonical minimal basis of minimal open neighbourhoods (Mathlib's nhdsKer {x} at each point). Kernel-reducible enumeration gives the exact table #(0)=2, #(1)=2, #(2)=10, #(3)=142. A quantitative sandwich then shows that the discrete fiber 2^(2^N − N) dominates: for N ≥ 2 the remaining fibers contribute at most 2^(N(N−1) + 3·2^(N−2)), the ratio to the discrete term tends to 1, and for N ≥ 10 the total is at most twice the discrete term. The argument is a fiber decomposition: every finite topology is Alexandrov-discrete, the minimal neighbourhoods generate it, and the bases generating τ are exactly the families B with M_τ ⊆ B ⊆ {U | τ.IsOpen U}. The informal account is the companion note CARDB.md in this repository. The Lean source was written by AI agents under the direction and review of the author. There is no sorry outside the deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and Mathlib is the only Lake dependency.
entries.title: catskillsresearch/cardb

entries.abstract: Kernel-checked exact-constant results for the CHSH operator T = A₀B₀ + A₀B₁ + A₁B₀ − A₁B₁ of an arbitrary CHSH tuple (Mathlib's IsCHSHTuple: self-adjoint involutions with the A's commuting with the B's). (1) The Landau identity: in any *-ring, T² = 4 + [A₀,A₁]·[B₁,B₀] — the exact, representation-independent correction to the naive T² = 8·1 (chsh_mul_self). (2) Tsirelson's bound in norm form: ‖T‖ ≤ 2√2 for every CHSH tuple in every nontrivial unital real C*-normed algebra (chsh_norm_le). (3) The classical constant, exactly: if either party's pair commutes, ‖T‖ = 2 — not merely ≤ 2 (chsh_norm_of_comm). (4) Necessity of noncommutativity: any violation ‖T‖ > 2 forces A₀A₁ ≠ A₁A₀ and B₀B₁ ≠ B₁B₀ — noncommutativity within both parties is necessary for any violation of the classical bound (noncomm_of_chsh_norm_gt_two). (5) The exact constant of M₄(ℝ): in the l2 operator norm, 2√2 is the greatest element of the set of CHSH operator norms over 4×4 real matrices — an upper bound for every tuple, attained by an explicit real-Pauli tuple (chsh_opNorm_isGreatest), so the maximal violation 2√2 is possible, not just bounded. The witness side stays compared: the explicit quadruple is verified to be a genuine CHSH tuple, its CHSH operator has eigenvalue exactly 2√2 on the explicit nonzero vector (1,0,0,1) and l2 operator norm exactly 2√2; the ordered star-ring bounds T ≤ (2√2)·1 and (commutative case) T ≤ 2 and the strict gap 2 < 2√2 complete the picture. A falsification is compared alongside: the saturating tuple's T² is not c·1 for ANY real c (chsh_sq_ne quantifies over every scalar), so the scalar-square route to the norm is closed for every scalar; the norm results here go through the C*-identity (and, for the generic bound, the Landau identity) instead.

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem of Legat, Yuan and Parrilo, "Low-Rank Univariate Sum of Squares Has No Spurious Local Minima" (SIAM J. Optim. 33(3), 2023). For a real univariate polynomial p and a pair of polynomials u = (u₁, u₂), consider the quadratically penalized Burer–Monteiro objective f_p(u) = ‖σ(u) - p‖² with σ(u) = u₁² + u₂², the norm coming from any inner product on ℝ[x]. The formalized theorem states that if p is a sum of two squares (which is the case for any nonnegative  univariate polynomial) and u is a second-order critical point of f_p (vanishing gradient and positive semidefinite Hessian, Definition 3.1 of the paper), then σ(u) = p, equivalently f_p(u) = 0; hence every SOCP, and in particular every local minimum, is a global minimum. The development follows the paper's proof: the gcd decomposition u = a·u₀ with u₀ coprime, the observation that σ(u₀) has no real roots, a Bézout-based "hgroup" lemma writing a sum of squares p as g·q + s·σ(u₀) with s a sum of squares when g and σ(u₀) are coprime, the factor-peeling argument that replaces the quadratic factors of a shared with σ(u₀) by X², and the final certificate argument combining the first- and second-order conditions.
entries.title: yuanchenyang/lean_low_rank_univariate_sos

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of Sendov's conjecture, and of its Phelps-Rodriguez strengthening, in full generality: if every zero of a complex polynomial p of degree n >= 2 lies in the closed unit disk, then every zero a of p has a critical point of p within distance 1 of it, and within distance strictly less than 1 unless |a| = 1 and p is a scalar multiple of z^n - a^n. The proof is by contradiction. Degrees 2 to 4 fall to an elementary integral computation; degree 5 upward goes through two estimates on the same integral -- a polar channel and an origin channel -- which are shown to be incompatible, reducing the theorem to a single numerical inequality. That inequality is discharged by exact rational Bernstein certificates, generated outside Lean and re-verified inside it, in both of its ranges: per-degree certificates for 5 <= n <= 100, and, for n >= 101, a single degree-58 certificate closing the one-variable inequality that the analytic large-degree reduction leaves behind. The boundary case |a| = 1 is proved separately from a reciprocal identity, and it is there that the equality classification is extracted. Nothing here is claimed to be new: the informal proof being formalized is a digestion of Lech Mazur's proof, which had already been formalized in Lean, so this is a second and independently checkable machine-checked proof of Sendov's conjecture, whose additional content is the Phelps-Rodriguez equality case. The Lean source was written by an AI agent under the direction and review of the author. There is no sorry outside the two deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, no native_decide, and no floating point in any statement or proof.
entries.title: teorth/sendov

entries.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the vertex-gap obstruction at (k,d2) = (2,2) (label thm:22, Theorem 3.4 in the current compilation) from the campaign paper "A Vertex-Gap Obstruction for Low-Degree Strip Pairs in the Plane Jacobian Conjecture": for polynomials P, Q in K[x,y] over a field K of characteristic not in {2,3,5}, supported in the normalized type-(2,2) Newton strips along (1,2) with [P,Q] = x^2, the block coefficients satisfy a3 = 0 and a2^2*a6 = 0 - so the generic chart a2*a6 != 0 of the strip family is empty (VertexGap22, plus the side-symmetric companion VertexGap22_swapped in the mirrored labels). Also formalized: the arithmetic corner-enumeration lemma behind the vertex normalization (lem:enum, Lemma 2.2; CornerEnumeration) and the side-symmetric form of the gap condition, hypothesis (ii) as corrected by the erratum recorded in Section 8 (GapConditionSideSymm).  The theorem is the mechanism that empties the generic chart of the (8,28) strip subcase in the campaign on the plane Jacobian problem at Newton-degree pair (72,108).

entries.abstract: A kernel-checked chirality package for the Padovan substitution (0 ↦ 1, 1 ↦ 2, 2 ↦ 01 on Fin 3; its incidence matrix has characteristic polynomial x³ − x − 1, an orientation fact that is not used or compared). Three compared theorems, all at the iterate-factor level — they quantify over factors of the concrete words S^[n] [x], never over an abstract subshift. (1) The successor invariant: in every positive iterate from any seed, the letter 0 ("a") is immediately followed by 1 ("b"). (2) Chirality: the word 20 ("ca") is a factor of an iterate while its reversal 02 ("ac") is a factor of no iterate from any seed — the factor language reads differently backwards — proved from the invariant, with no enumeration on the ac side. (3) No palindromic factor: no factor of length ≥ 4 of any iterate from any seed (including the zeroth iterate) is a palindrome, via a complete length-≤5 window certificate for the seed a together with the index shift S [0] = [1], S [1] = [2], which exhibits every seed's iterate as a seed-a iterate.
entries.title: stalex444/arithmetic-of-time

entries.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem A (ODE rigidity, all weights; label thm:ode, Theorem 6.1 in the current compilation of the campaign paper): if polynomials A, C over an integral domain of characteristic zero and an integer weight nu >= 1 satisfy A*C' - nu*A'*C = c for a nonzero constant c, then deg A <= 1 (TheoremA).  Also a standalone positive-characteristic strengthening extracted from the same proof (TheoremA_charP): the same conclusion over a domain of characteristic p under the degree bounds nu*deg A < p and deg C < p.  The theorem is the rigidity engine of the depth-two block analysis in the campaign on the plane Jacobian problem at Newton-degree pair (72,108).

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of the theorem that every torsion-free Abelian group of cardinality continuum admits a Hausdorff countably compact group topology in which every convergent sequence is eventually constant, and constructs a commutative Tychonoff countably compact cancellative topological monoid that is not a group, giving a negative answer to Wallace's question.

entries.abstract: The Jordan curve theorem, formalized in Lean 4 against Mathlib: a continuous injective map from the circle into the plane has a complement with exactly two connected components. The hypothesis is bare continuity and injectivity — no smoothness, piecewise-linearity or rectifiability — which is what makes the theorem hard and what separates it from the polygonal case. The proof follows Maehara's reduction to the Brouwer fixed point theorem, via a crossing lemma for transversal paths in a rectangle and the fact that every component has the curve as its boundary, together with a farthest-pair normalization that pins down exactly one bounded component. Because Mathlib has no Brouwer fixed point theorem at the pinned revision, Brouwer is built here from the ground up: covering-space path lifting for the circle giving π₁(S¹) ≅ ℤ, then no-retraction of the disk onto its boundary, then Brouwer on the disk by ray-retraction, then the general nonempty-compact-convex case by nearest-point projection. The statement is expressed in Mathlib's own vocabulary. The proof is sorry-free and depends on Lean's three standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound) and nothing else.
entries.title: rkirov/jordan_pick

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that there are absolute constants c > 0 and p₀ such that, for every prime p ≥ p₀, the minimum size m(p) of a set A ⊆ 𝔽_p with |A| ≥ 2 and no uniquely represented sum satisfies m(p) ≥ c (log p / log log p)².  Here representations are unordered two-element multisets from A, repeated summands are allowed, and "no unique sum" means that every such multiset has a distinct equal-sum mate.

entries.abstract: `PrimeGapsLib` is an evolving codebase aimed at housing results about gaps in primes. The flagship result thus far is that pairs of primes are separated by at most 246 infinitely often, conditional on the Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem. The 246 proof was generated collaboratively between human formalisers at Axiom Math and AxiomProver, their in-house theorem proving system. Community feedback and contributions are welcome!
